title: Quality-engineering change plan
description: What a change commits to before it is written: which requirement it serves, which test decides it, and how it fails. The value is not the document -- it is that the three questions have to be answerable before the code exists. A change that cannot name the test that decides it is a change nobody can tell is working, and that is discovered at the end of the work rather than the start. Validate with scripts/qe_gate.py --plan <file>.

summary.description: One sentence on what changes in behaviour, not what changes in the files.

requirements.description: Registry ids this change serves. A new requirement is listed here with new: true and is added to the registry in the same commit.

verification.description: The tests that decide this change. Named before the code is written, because a test chosen afterwards tends to be a test the code already passes.

decides.description: What this test would catch that nothing else does. If the honest answer is 'nothing', the test is coverage rather than verification and should be replaced.

failure_mode.description: What goes wrong in production if this change is wrong. The question that decides how much care the change deserves.

blast_radius.description: How far a mistake reaches. 'funds' means the change can move money and deserves the strictest review.

rollback.description: How this is undone if it is wrong in production. 'Revert the commit' is a valid answer only when no state has migrated.

gates_run.description: Gate ids from qe.config.json that were run locally before pushing.

allOf.title: A defect fix carries a REG- entry
allOf.description: Every production defect gets a permanent regression test. Fixing without recording is how the same bug returns in six months and is investigated from scratch.

allOf.title: A security finding carries a SEC- entry
A change that can move money states its blast radius and its rollback
allOf.description: Not ceremony: these are the two questions an operator asks at 3am, and the time to answer them is while the change is being designed.

allOf.title: A refactor that changes no behaviour still names the tests that prove it
allOf.description: The claim 'no behaviour change' is exactly the claim a test can check, and the refactor that quietly changed one is the reason this is not waived.
